title: Administrator
description:
Sophia at Avocet Legal Careers is pleased to present an interesting opportunity for an experienced Administrator to join a specialist law firm, just outside Chudleigh.

This is a fast-paced, high-volume administrative role at the centre of a national claims and conciliation process - ideal for someone with tenacity, sharp organisational instincts and genuine resilience under pressure.

About the Client

Our client is a long-established and highly respected regulated and specialist law firm who provide their clients with fully comprehensive legal advice and representation, effectively operating as an in-house legal department for each client.

The firm is the lead conciliator and arbitrator for a national conciliation service and holds standing counsel status for a major industry federation.

You will manage the receipt, checking and verification of claim forms, working to a structured checklist to ensure claim packs are complete and ready for conciliation within set timeframes. Alongside processing new claims, you'll manage an ongoing caseload of existing claims and a high daily volume of queries.

You'll correspond directly with claimants to chase missing information, liaise with traders under a defined process to report complaints and gather submissions, and work closely with conciliators once packs are ready, actioning any follow-up requests for additional information. Administrator Responsibilities
- Receiving, checking and verifying claim forms against a set checklist
- Corresponding with claimants to obtain missing information and complete claim packs
- Managing new claims alongside an ongoing caseload of existing claims and queries
- Handling a high daily volume of email queries across multiple inboxes
- Drafting own correspondence with claimants and traders
- Liaising with traders under a set process to report complaints and obtain submissions
- Liaising with conciliators once packs are ready, and actioning requests for further information
- Extensive diary management throughout the claims and conciliation process

Administrator Requirements
- Strong administrative background with excellent organisational skills
- Confident, resilient communicator, comfortable managing complaints and difficult conversations
- Able to act effectively as a go-between for clients and lawyers
- Comfortable managing high volumes of correspondence and multiple email inboxes
- Strong written communication skills and ability to draft own correspondence
- Excellent attention to detail and ability to work to strict timeframes
- Own vehicle required due to the rural location of the office

Benefits
- Salary DOE
- Pension plan
- 20 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays
- Christmas shutdown
- Free onsite parking

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate will be a robust, unflappable administrator with a genuine appetite for a busy, complaint-heavy environment. You'll be organised, quick to prioritise, and comfortable being the calm point of contact between claimants, traders, conciliators and the legal team.

Process electronic inbound referrals from GP's and other healthcare organisations using patient record systems. Booking and managing of patient appointments. Deal with routine patient enquiries. Ensure that electronic tasks are completed in a timely manner. Assist in monitoring generic email accounts. Send text reminder messages/emails to patients. Supporting Senior Administrative colleagues. Attending administrative and clinical meetings as required, which may occasionally be outside of core working hours. General office duties, such as post, scanning etc. Use the e-Referrals system (eRS) and the Electronic Patient Record systems (EMIS & SystmOne) to access inbound referrals and associated clinical documents booked in the Sentinel Healthcare clinical services. Liaise with local Referral Management Centres, GP surgeries and other external organisations as necessary. Using own judgement bring any GP referrals which may be inappropriate to the Clinician(s) attention. Ensure that inbound referrals are appropriately actioned i.e. accepted or rejected. Assist in co-ordinating the utilisation of booking slots across service areas, ensuring that capacity is fully utilised. Any under-utilisation to be reported promptly to the Operations Manager, so that appropriate action can be taken in advance. Ensure that relevant reminders (either by SMS, email or letter, where appropriate) have been sent to patients informing them of appointments. Assist in using the patient record system to ensure that clinical reports and templates are re-produced and sent to GPs (and patients if required) following consultations. Liaise with GP(s) or their team(s) when removing patients from the waiting lists as per protocols Have a sympathetic and caring manner when dealing with patients, ensuring all queries are handled timely, efficiently and effectively. Deal with telephone queries from both internal and external agencies in a professional manner in accordance with GDPR and statutory policies and procedures. To deal with all enquiries and complaints promptly and sympathetically and inform Senior Management of any problems immediately. Record accurate patient messages and complete information using the patient record system in a timely manner. Request hospital patient case notes (where requested by clinicians) ensuring that relevant clinical documentation (e.g. referral letter, x-rays, other diagnostic results and other supporting information) is available to the clinical teams in the patient record system. Maintain patient case notes and other documentation in good order and arrange return appropriately and in a timely manner. Assist in arranging and attending MDT meetings (where necessary) and ensure that patient notes, investigations and radiology images are available. Work flexibly and collaboratively with colleagues and help to develop a positive, supportive culture. Be prepared to work at various locations to provide appropriate administrative support to clinical teams as required. Attend and contribute positively and creatively to Administration Meetings. Demonstrate a positive, can-do attitude in the workplace. Ensure that resources are used efficiently and help to identify cost savings. Attend and represent Sentinel at external meetings as required Maintain an efficient electronic filing system. Responsible for covering colleagues during periods of annual leave and sickness. description: Supporting the Clinical teams across the Haematology and Oncology Day Case Units, collaborating with key staff members to ensure smooth implementation of complex patient appointment pathways. For more detail about the main duties of this role, please see the job description section below. As a key member of the Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, you will be joining an exceptional team working together to help our patients to stay healthy, when they need it most. For more information on the Job Description and Responsibilities please click the link below. More detail about the role Working Pattern: 37.5 hours to be worked across 4 days including Saturday and bank holiday rotations Interview Date: To Be Confirmed For further information please contact: Jasmine Dorothy, Admin Line Manager on jasmine.dorothy@nhs.net This is an internal vacancy for Royal Devon employees, therefore Bank workers are currently not eligible to apply for this vacancy. This is a fixed term contract . For current NHS employees this post could be a secondment opportunity. As an inclusive employer, the Royal Devon values diversity and is committed to creating a culture of inclusivity where everyone can be themselves and reach their full potential. We believe in fostering a sense of belonging and actively encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, cultures, and abilities. We recognise the advantages of having a diverse workforce that reflects the communities we serve. Preference will be given to staff with Priority and 'At Risk' status including NHS At Risk staff throughout Devon. The Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust reserves the right to close vacancy when sufficient applications have been received. The Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust was established in April 2022, bringing together the expertise of both the Royal Devon and Exeter NHS Foundation Trust and Northern Devon Healthcare NHS Trust. Benefits We will work together to maintain a culture that develops and supports you and your team. This might include funding for a care certificate, a degree or leadership qualifications. Or it might include days off to study, engage in CPD or rotational placements to help you hone your skills. Wherever you are heading in the NHS, we'll help you get there. Looking after you is important to us. We strive to help our staff create a healthy work-life balance through flexible working schemes and our family friendly policies. If you're starting out in the NHS, you'll start with 27 days paid annual leave (plus bank holidays), rising to 33 days plus bank holidays. You'll benefit from access to our own comprehensive occupational health services, including counselling, onsite wellbeing activities and groups. Salary is not the only financial benefit You'll have access to an extensive range of staff discounts on shopping, fitness and leisure options and you can spread the cost of technology and home appliance purchases from major retailers. You will also have access to other benefits including: National discount services such as the Blue Light Card and Health Service Discounts. Salary sacrifice options including our OFSTED rated outstanding nursery onsite at Exeter Car lease schemes. The NHS Pension scheme (one of the most generous and comprehensive in the UK). Cycle to work scheme These are just a few of the benefits available if the role is something you are interested in, we'd love to hear from you.
